---
title: "6 · Applications of Scrambling"
---

In the earlier chapters randomness is something to characterize. Here it is
deployed on purpose, because the same Haar second moment that fixes the Page
curve also underwrites protocols for learning and benchmarking quantum systems
and sharpens a thought experiment about black holes.

Classical shadows use random single-copy measurements followed by an analytic
inversion of the measurement channel to predict many observables of an unknown
state from few copies, with a sample cost controlled by a shadow norm that grows
as $3^k$ for $k$-local Pauli observables. Randomized benchmarking averages over
random Clifford sequences so that gate-dependent noise twirls into a single
depolarizing channel, whose strength is read from the exponential decay of the
survival probability and reported as an average fidelity. Both rest on the same
twirl, the second-moment average that replaces a complicated operator by a
combination of the identity and the swap.

The Hayden-Preskill thought experiment applies that mathematics to a black hole
modelled as a fast scrambler. Information dropped in can be reconstructed from
the outgoing radiation almost as soon as it is absorbed, provided one already
holds the radiation emitted earlier, a statement the decoupling theorem makes
precise and which reuses the Page-curve estimate of Chapter 3. Tripartite mutual
information turns the same average into a scrambling diagnostic, while the
fragility of GHZ-state metrology shows the cost of storing information
non-locally, where the loss of a single qubit erases a Heisenberg-scaling signal.

## Notebooks in this part

- [The shadow channel](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_shadow_channel.ipynb), inverting the measurement channel, the heart of classical shadows.
- [Classical shadows in action](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_numerical_shadows.ipynb), estimating observables from random measurements.
- [Randomized benchmarking](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_numerical_randomized_benchmarking.ipynb), extracting gate fidelity from an exponential decay.
- [Tripartite mutual information](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_tripartite_mutual_information.ipynb), a quantitative diagnostic of scrambling.
- [Fragility of GHZ metrology](../notebooks/ch6/solution_ch6_greenberger_horne_zeilinger_fragility.ipynb), Heisenberg-scaling sensitivity destroyed by a single lost qubit.
